sources.title: Canadian Institute of Ukrainian Studies: Krivichians
sources.note: Geographical extent, principal cities and later incorporation in Rus’. No simple modern ethnic descent assertion adopted.

sources.title: Izborsk Museum: Izborsk, an open city
sources.note: Section Grad krivichei: turn seventh/eighth settlement, approximately 16 square metre ground-level log houses, corner stone/clay heaters; early-horizon spindle whorls and harvesting tools; African dirhams minted 792/3 but circulation 800 to 825. Museum’s ethnic certainty not repeated.

sources.title: Z. D. Yushchenko after I. V. Islanova: Pskov Long Barrow Culture
sources.note: Academic project; author credit at end. Sections location, chronology, material complex, economy and origins. Archaeological category explicitly distinguished from ethnonym; eighth-century bead phase II B, other livelihoods broader culture.

sources.title: Russian Academy of Sciences: Izborsk archaeological investigations
sources.note: Printed page 33, summary of Sedov 2007. Direct text retrieved by open line 30: varied house forms/material interpreted as Slavic, Baltic and Baltic-Finnic presence; eighth/tenth proto-town; later tenth/eleventh timber citadel and wheel pottery.

sources.title: Institute of Archaeology: Islanova’s study of settlements and cemeteries in Archaeology of the Moscow Region 19
sources.note: 19 May 2023, first two research-summary paragraphs only. Southern Msta/Volga watershed: 65 burial complexes, 36 settlements; thin disturbed deposits and marshy access; spatial model identified settlement near Ivankovo 1 to 3. Counts are research inventory.

sources.title: National Library of Russia: Laurentian Chronicle, manuscript of 1377, folio 7
sources.note: Indexed original directly checked through query site.expositions.nlr.ru/LaurentianCodex "кривичехъ" "северех". Image index 19 corresponds to folio 7 according to library event list. Public sample explicitly from library transliteration, not diplomatic glyph reproduction or contemporary eighth-century writing. Shared with Severians; all derivation counted together.

sources.title: Arkadii Zhukovsky: Siverianians, Internet Encyclopedia of Ukraine
sources.note: Desna and upper Seim/Sula/Psol/Vorskla geography; Khazar tribute and chronicle account of Oleh in 884; last chronicle mention 1024. Do not repeat uninhabited steppe assertion or turn disappearance of name into extinction.

sources.title: O. V. Sukhobokov: Bytytsia hillfort, Encyclopedia of Modern Ukraine
sources.note: Excavator’s entry: high Psel terrace, over seven hectares, about 6000 square metres excavated, over 60 dwellings, around 250 metal objects and two hoards. Mid-eighth to turn eighth/ninth chronology. Ethnic interpretations explicitly attributed.

sources.title: O. V. Sukhobokov: Early stages of the culture of the chronicle Severians
sources.note: East European Archaeological Journal 3(4), 2000. Direct fetch timed out; full indexed original opening and figure captions checked. Opening paragraphs describe handmade pots/bowls as majority plus local wheel pottery; archaeology/ethnicity and cultural sequence explicitly debated. Figure 6 utility structure 20 labelled tondyr, but no unsupported recipe adopted.

sources.title: Sergiy Gorbanenko: Palaeoethnobotanical spectrum of Bytytsia hillfort
sources.note: Author-posted English abstract for Drevnosti 2011 volume 10 pages 242 to 247. Full indexed original; direct fetch failed. Millet, barley, bread wheat, rye, emmer, oats, einkorn and spelt impressions, plus weeds. Listed counts do not sum to stated 94, so totals omitted; inferred double/triple-field system not adopted.

sources.title: I. I. Lyapushkin: On the dwellings of the eastern Slavs of the Dnipro left bank in the eighth to tenth centuries
sources.note: Full original scholarly article reproduced, Kratkie soobshcheniya IIMK volume 68. Paragraph beginning But in 1932 to 1954: over 50 sunken houses and about 100 utility buildings at Novotroitske, ninth century. Author’s excavated observations reject covered internal passages. Counts describe excavated features across occupation, not simultaneous census.

sources.title: Great Russian Encyclopedia: Novotroitske hillfort
sources.note: Full indexed original checked with exact URL and Novotroickoe query. Ninth-century site, metal woodworking and farming tools, bone points and astragals with incised geometric compositions. Game or ritual attribution not asserted; Pecheneg destruction theory omitted.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Imported 700 to 800 footprint: 27.39807 to 38.46098 E, 56.06157 to 60.87120 N. Southern centres Polotsk and Smolensk omitted; overview explicit. No alias to later Polotsk/Pskov/Novgorod states or modern nations. Long Barrow Culture treated as distinct archaeological category and mixed-origin interpretation. No artificial midpoint years.

Imported 700 to 800 footprint: 29.21609 to 33.49293 E, 49.11187 to 51.45240 N. Omits eastern Seim/Kursk, much Psel/Vorskla territory and Bytytsia/Novotroitske. Overview and first site passages explicit. Eastern Slavic Severians distinct from Danubian similarly named peoples. Ninth-century Novotroitske and chronicle account 884 marked later; no unsupported attackers or writing invented.
